title: Claude Code enables free AI-powered terminal with open-source #claudecode #freeai #aidevelopment
description:
Claude Code enabled free, unlimited usage by leveraging a GitHub tool that simulates Claude Code’s environment while using free AI models. This solution provides access to AI capabilities at 80-90% of Cloud Code’s performance without any cost, appealing to over 20,000 developers who have adopted this simple, quick setup method.

The approach involves connecting to free AI providers such as NVIDIA NIM or OpenRouter for access to models like DeepSeek, Kimi, and GLM, or running models locally via Ollama with a compatible GPU. This innovation disrupts conventional paid Claude Code services by democratizing access to advanced AI tools, lowering barriers for developers, startups, and AI enthusiasts.

By offering a free alternative with minimal setup time, this method accelerates experimentation and development in AI-driven applications, supporting broader adoption across the tech community. It highlights ongoing community-driven efforts to make AI services more accessible and cost-effective.

For the type of projects I build I wouldn't trust a tool that's only 90% as good.
I guess if you're just doing little python scripts or a flask app, sure. It's probably fine for just whipping up basic stuff. But for me, even when a new model comes out I go back and have the new stronger model review and improve the projects I built. There's no point using a weaker model if you don't have to.
90% as good means 10% crap. And I don't want even 1% of it to be crap.
